question: Should RFC 0013 formally adopt these three lifecycle sidecars as a host-neutral contract, or should recovery-point composition, final handoff, and restored admission remain outside the completed SQLite snapshot RFC until core implementation and ownership are separately approved?
rationale: The proposed documents define new cross-boundary obligations and compatibility expectations rather than correcting an established implementation contract; source evidence alone cannot decide the intended permanent public boundary.

options.title: Adopt a narrow sidecar boundary
options.body: Accept the owner/host split while retaining explicit non-goals for ingress fencing, wake, storage transport, and provider-specific lifecycle control.

options.title: Defer lifecycle sidecars
options.body: Keep RFC 0013 limited to one-database SQLite artifacts and revisit these contracts only with a sponsored implementation plan and designated owners.

recommendation.title: Adopt a narrow sidecar boundary
recommendation.body: Accept the owner/host split while retaining explicit non-goals for ingress fencing, wake, storage transport, and provider-specific lifecycle control.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied context identifies Vincent's snapshot and cooperative-suspension work as the existing contracts that the proposed sidecars compose.
